Harry Bush was an English cricketer who played first-class cricket in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Here’s what is known about him:

### **Basic Information:**
- **Full Name:** Harry Bush
- **Born:** 1874 (exact date unknown)
- **Died:** 1946 (exact date unknown)
- **Major Teams:** Gloucestershire, London County
- **Playing Role:** Wicketkeeper and batsman

### **Career Overview:**
- Bush was a wicketkeeper who played for **Gloucestershire** between **1899 and 1904**.
- He also played for **London County**, a team organized by W.G. Grace, in **1900 and 1901**.
- His first-class career spanned **23 matches**, in which he scored **350 runs** at an average of **10.30**, with a highest score of **38**.
- As a wicketkeeper, he took **23 catches and made 13 stumpings**.

### **Notable Matches & Performances:**
- Bush was part of Gloucestershire’s team during a period when the county was competitive but not dominant.
- He played alongside legendary cricketers like **W.G. Grace** and **Gilbert Jessop** during his time at Gloucestershire.
- His best performance with the bat came in **1900** when he scored **38 runs** against Surrey.

### **Later Life & Legacy:**
- After retiring from first-class cricket, Bush continued to be involved in the sport at a local level.
- He died in **1946**, but details about his later life are scarce.

### **Summary:**
Harry Bush was a modest but competent wicketkeeper who had a brief first-class career in the early 1900s. While not a standout performer, he contributed to Gloucestershire and London County during his playing days. His career was overshadowed by more prominent figures of the era, but he remains a part of cricket history.
